questions.q: Is a Priority 1 incident automatically a Major Incident?
options: No — Priority 1 means Critical by the Impact/Urgency matrix, but Major Incident Management is a separate, heavier process reserved for incidents crossing a defined severity threshold
Yes, every Priority 1 incident is automatically a Major Incident
Major Incident Management only applies to Priority 4 incidents
Priority and Major Incident status are the same field on the incident table
questions.explain: Priority 1 and Major Incident status are tracked separately — a Priority 1 ticket can be handled by the ordinary process without triggering MIM.

questions.q: What are the real values typically held by major_incident_state?
options: New, In Progress, Resolved
Low, Medium, High
None, Candidate, Declared
Open, On Hold, Closed
questions.explain: major_incident_state is distinct from the ordinary incident state field and tracks None, Candidate, and Declared.

questions.q: Why should hitting the Major Incident threshold make an incident a Candidate rather than automatically Declared?
options: Automatic declaration is actually required by ServiceNow and cannot be changed
A human review avoids false positives — e.g. a Priority 1 affecting one VIP user that doesn't actually need a war room — and preserves trust in the MIM process
Candidates cannot be reviewed by a major incident manager
Declared incidents are not allowed to have a Priority value
questions.explain: Automatic declaration produces false positives and erodes trust the first time MIM fires unnecessarily; a human makes the actual call.

questions.q: What does a declared Major Incident use that a standard incident typically doesn't?
options: A dedicated war room or bridge call, plus a fixed stakeholder communication cadence
A Hold Reason field
A Priority Lookup Rule
An Assignment Group
questions.explain: War rooms/bridges and a fixed communication cadence (e.g. every 15-30 minutes) are MIM-specific coordination practices.

questions.q: What does a Major Incident require after resolution that a standard incident doesn't?
options: A Resolution Code
A formal, documented post-incident review covering the timeline, what worked, what didn't, and follow-up changes
Close Notes
An Assignment Group
questions.explain: Resolution Code and Close Notes apply to any incident; the formal post-incident review is a MIM-specific requirement.
